headline: Highest risk is prompt-injection via OpenMetadata’s MCP/API/webhook surfaces into a local-only Pathway pipeline; other risks are mostly constrained by Pathway’s no-write/no-network profile.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: OpenMetadata exposes MCP, APIs, events, and webhooks, so it can emit content that Pathway may ingest if wired together. Pathway has no clipboard, stdin/stdout, or file surfaces, which lowers direct hijack risk, but the pair still has a plausible shared-channel pathway via orchestration. Uncertainty about the exact integration escalates to medium.
conditions: IF Pathway is configured to consume OpenMetadata webhook/event payloads as instructions, injection becomes active.
IF an operator manually copies OpenMetadata output into Pathway inputs, prompt-style hijacking is possible.
mitigations: Treat OpenMetadata outputs as untrusted data, not instructions.
Add a schema-only parser for any OpenMetadata payloads.
Disable any free-text command fields in the integration.
Require human review before Pathway acts on catalog text.
requires-engineering: add provenance tags from OpenMetadata to Pathway inputs.

B_data_leakage.rationale: OpenMetadata touches governance, lineage, semantics, and memory/tribal knowledge, so sensitive operational metadata may be present. Pathway shows no filesystem read/write, no network egress, and no API calls, so there is no obvious exfiltration path from the pair. The remaining risk is limited to accidental exposure through whatever external integration is added.
conditions: IF Pathway is later connected to an external sink or API, metadata leakage risk increases.
IF OpenMetadata stores sensitive governance records in fields Pathway ingests, those records may be copied into downstream outputs.
mitigations: Minimize sensitive fields sent from OpenMetadata to Pathway.
Mask identifiers before transfer.
Keep Pathway isolated from external sinks.
Review integration mappings for secret-bearing columns.
requires-engineering: enforce field-level allowlists.

C_capability_conflict.rationale: OpenMetadata can run multiple instances and uses APIs/MCP, but Pathway has no filesystem write, no git mutation, and no subprocess or shell execution. With no overlapping mutable resource exposed in the profiles, there is no credible write-write conflict pathway to arbitrate.
conditions: IF Pathway is reconfigured to write to the same mutable store as OpenMetadata, conflict risk would need reassessment.
mitigations: Keep Pathway read-only relative to OpenMetadata state.
Avoid shared writable directories.
Use separate service accounts.
Document ownership of any shared database tables.
requires-engineering: add locking if a shared mutable backend is introduced.

D_cascading_error.rationale: OpenMetadata can produce catalog, lineage, and governance outputs that Pathway could consume as upstream data. Pathway is a document-processing system, so if it treats those outputs as authoritative without verification, errors can cascade into downstream work products. The profiles do not show a built-in verification step, so medium is warranted.
conditions: IF Pathway uses OpenMetadata outputs as source-of-truth inputs without validation, cascading errors can propagate.
IF OpenMetadata emits stale or incorrect lineage metadata, Pathway may reproduce it downstream.
mitigations: Add validation against source systems before Pathway acts.
Require confidence labels on OpenMetadata-derived fields.
Route uncertain records to manual review.
Log provenance for every derived document.
requires-engineering: implement reconciliation checks.

E_compliance.rationale: OpenMetadata explicitly touches governance and memory/tribal knowledge, which can include regulated metadata, while Pathway’s profile shows no data classes touched and no network egress. There is no documented residency or certification mismatch in the profiles, so compliance risk is limited to configuration-specific handling rather than a default breach.
conditions: IF regulated data is stored in OpenMetadata and exported into Pathway outputs, compliance review is required.
IF deployment policy requires residency controls that are not configured on the OpenMetadata side, a mismatch may occur.
mitigations: Classify data before transfer.
Exclude regulated fields from Pathway inputs.
Confirm residency and retention settings on OpenMetadata.
Keep audit logs for transfers.
requires-engineering: add policy enforcement for regulated datasets.
